name: Rayl

open.name: Enterable surfaces
open.what: the field, the select, the checkbox, the toggle and the dialog that holds them
open.detail: This was the largest open item in the system and it is answered: a control that ACCEPTS input reads as enterable through a change of ground alone — surface/idle at cap + 24, rounding 8, padding 12, and the focus ring as the one stroke. Every measurement is read off the UI Control Blanks boards and all of it ships, so build with it rather than inventing. It is PROVISIONAL and not a RULE because Martijn has drawn it and has not yet seen it rendered. Do not write it into a document as settled until he has.

open.name: Component states
open.what: empty, error and skeleton now ship; loading was already the loading mark
open.detail: rayl-empty is a panel with nothing in it and an error is the same panel with different words, because nothing in the palette means error. rayl-skeleton is blocks where type will land and it does not move. Hover, pressed, disabled and focus were always covered by the tokens, and a wait is still rayl-solve. These are drawn rather than decided, so they move with the enterable surfaces above.

open.name: A check glyph
open.what: the icon set has no colour, so a ticked box and a failed panel show the same mark
open.detail: ON is carried by the ground — the box turns Bone the way every selected thing does — and the mark inside it is Plus turned 45 degrees, because that is the only glyph in the set that reads as a mark rather than an instruction. The empty panel's error twin shows the same glyph at 24. Two opposite meanings on one drawing is a real weakness and it wants either a nineteenth icon or a decision that the ground alone is enough. Do not draw a tick.

open.name: The scrim
open.what: the page behind a dialog, dimmed 20%
open.detail: 20% is the figure on the board and it is what ships. The colour is the darkest ground the mode has — Black in light, Deep Black in dark — because a scrim is a shadow: taking ink/primary would flip it to White in dark mode and lighten the page instead of dimming it. Only the light value was drawn; the dark one follows from that reasoning and has not been looked at.

open.name: Semantic colour
open.what: nothing means error, warning, success or info
open.detail: Every colour in the palette sits on one hue, so any of these is the brand's first hue break. Do not draft a palette colour in to stand for a state and do not borrow a red.

open.name: Deep Black #11110F
open.what: the dark-mode ground, and the one palette colour not on the approved frame
open.detail: It ships and it works. Either it joins the palette or dark mode grounds on a colour already in it.

open.name: Hover: the ladder or the token
open.what: two approved sources give a Paper base two different hovers
open.detail: The L* ladder says Bone, five steps away. surface/idle-hover says Off White, one step. Build with the tokens — they are what ships — but the disagreement is real and wants a decision.

open.name: A container's padding
open.what: "a container pads one step below the gap it sits in"
open.detail: It held when the page ran 72 and a band padded 48. The page runs 96 now and the band still pads 48, where the rule would say 72. Do not apply it to anything new.

open.name: 96 on the spacing scale
open.what: the page rhythm is 96 and the scale as written stops at 72
open.detail: 96 steps by 12 like every other member and is what rayl-page actually uses, so it is listed. Confirm it is a member rather than a page-only figure.

open.name: The 8 radius
open.what: every control rounds 8; the board's own ladder is 4, 12, 24
open.detail: 8 is measured off the approved UI rather than the demo, and where the two disagree the UI wins. Worth confirming the ladder gains an 8.

open.name: The Rayl look
open.what: it ships as is-look; dark mode and one alpha in it are not drawn
open.detail:
Measured at 966:2041, re-struck on the palette and shipped opt-in, on the card and nothing inside it — the file's second scale, the 20-tall rows, is deliberately not in Rayl. What is provisional is dark: nobody drew it. The rim and the lift survive by changing colour rather than alpha, but the press does not — light darkens its corner by about 12 L* and dark has 5.2 of headroom in total, so the press alpha is raised from its measured 30% to 70% and still reaches only 3.3. That one number is invented. The alternative is no press in dark at all, which is honest and reads flatter than light.

Also standing: Bone is the rim, and Bone is what selection is painted in. A card rimmed in Bone and a selected control are the same colour. Bone was taken because it is the only step that keeps the bowl (5.5 L* against the drawn 5.7, where the alternative gives 1.6) and keeps the 108 rows on the step they are drawn on. Worth revisiting if the two ever meet on a page.

open.name: Shadows
open.what: the Rayl look needs two, and nothing else in the system has one
open.detail: Section 2 forbids a shadow on the mark, section 5 makes every boundary out of a change of ground, and the loading mark carries an opaque tile on every face so that nothing is drawn at part strength. A shadow is drawn at part strength. Same question as the scrim: does the system have shadows now, or does the look get them and nothing else? Nothing may take one until this is answered.

open.name: The reveal button's label
open.what: White #FFFFFF on the approved frame, Off White in the ink table
open.detail: One value, two approved sources. Ask before using either.

open.name: The loading mark's timing
open.what: rayl-solve runs on numbers and a curve that are not the system's
open.detail: A turn is 480ms with no beat between turns, a scramble turn 480ms, and it sits on the solved mark for 960ms — where the system's numbers are 280, 90, 220 and 2400. The curve is cubic-bezier(0.5, 0.14, 0.36, 0.79) where the system's one curve is cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1). Every value was picked by Martijn on the bench, watching whole turns; no reason is recorded beyond that, and none is invented here. The component runs correctly on the system's numbers — set data-turn, data-gap, data-scramble, data-hold and data-ease to put any instance back on them. This is the second easing in the system, and the whole argument of section 7 is that there is one. It is on this list rather than hidden in a stylesheet.

open.name: A colour change runs 120ms
open.what: the ground under a control moves at 120ms ease-out, not on the system's curve
open.detail: Every documented movement is 280ms on cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1), and section 7 says both surfaces move together on the same duration and curve. The shipped controls do not: a hover's colour change is 120ms ease-out while the label rolls at 280ms. It was in two places when it was first written down. The thirteen controls took it as the house value and it is now in eleven, which is worth knowing before deciding: this is no longer a stray, it is the system's second easing in practice. Either it joins the system as the value a ground moves on, or every one of the eleven changes.

open.name: Magnetism on buttons
open.what: the slider's lean, on everything that is its own target
open.detail:
The nub has leaned toward an approaching cursor since it was built and nothing else did. Buttons do now, on the nub's own range and strength — 104 and 0.6 — so no value was invented there.

Two things were changed after seeing it: every button in range leaned at once, which made a panel read as a row of things all asking to be clicked, and it moved too far. Now the nearest button in range leans and every other one lets go, and it moves at most 4.5 rather than 12 — three quarters of a cluster's gap, so a control never comes close to reaching its neighbour. The nub keeps 12 because it has nothing beside it.

Then three bugs, all found by measuring rather than by looking. The cap was a clamp on a bigger curve and it caught across 78% of the range, so the button jumped to its full lean on approach and sat there — the falloff is the shape itself now, peaking at 6 at half the range. The cached centres were never dropped when the real face landed and every button re-rendered wider, so on load the pull came from left of the button. And two buttons traded the lean pixel by pixel along the line between them, so a 6 band of hysteresis holds it.

What leans is what is its own target: the button, the reveal button, an option cell in an unjoined group, and the two on-or-off controls. What does not is what sits inside a block — a joined bar and every cell in it, and an item in an open menu. A block that drifts at a passing cursor reads as the whole row coming loose.

The select face is the one still unsettled: it is a button in the markup and it opens a list rather than doing something, and it currently does not lean.

Still provisional because it is the first thing in Rayl that moves without being touched, and section 7 is one movement.

open.name: Transparency
open.what: the scrim behind a dialog is the first thing in Rayl drawn at part strength
open.detail: Everything else in the system is flat and opaque — it is why the loading mark carries a tile on every face rather than fading, and why the palette is fifteen solid steps. A dialog has to dim what is behind it, so --rayl-scrim is a 20% mix and it is the right answer for that job. What is not decided is whether transparency is now a thing the system has, or one exception a dialog gets. Nothing else may fade until that is answered.

open.name: An array as a ground
open.what: the array can sit behind or in front of content, and nothing says how
open.detail: Section 11 already calls data-motion="still" the right choice for a header or a background, and then never says how to place one. The system has no layering vocabulary at all: z-index appears six times in core.css and every one is inside a component. So a background array today means hand-rolled position, inset and stacking, re-decided on every page, which is what layout primitives exist to prevent. Three things have to be answered before the primitive can be drawn. Is a background forced to still, or may it wave under text? What colour is type over an array — the ink flip works off a single L* and an array is a gradient sheet with bodies moving across it, so there is nothing to test. And does foreground mean over-and-clipped, like a masthead, or over-and-transparent, which the bodies being opaque makes a different question again.

open.name: The fonts
open.what: Azeret and Concrette here are TRIAL cuts
open.detail: Fine for internal work and prototypes. The licensed files have to replace them before anything built with this goes public.

open.name: CMYK
open.what: the printed values are arithmetic, not a profile conversion
open.detail: Fine on screen, not fine at a printer.

note: Never write a hex in a build. Name a token; it resolves per mode.

display.role: titles and subheads, 24 and up only
display.optical size: S ships; M and XL exist

label.use: names a section, and nothing else

meaning.6: parts of one control — buttons in a cluster, a stepper's digits
meaning.12: things in a document: blocks on the page, frames in a field
meaning.24: a group led by nothing larger than a 24
meaning.36: a group led by a 36; three columns of a split
meaning.48: a group led by a 48 or a 72; two columns of a split

meaning.8: a control — button, option cell, card, swatch
meaning.24: a container — a rail, a frame, a panel
meaning.half the height: anything meant to read as fully round

stagger.what: one character to the next, compressed so a roll never runs past 400ms

press up.what: and coming back — deliberately slower than down

a line returns.what: before a swapped line goes back to what it was

Page.rayl-page: the app or panel column: ground, 72 rhythm, 520 wide
Page.rayl-page is-wide: the same at 960, for a page that has to breathe
Page.rayl-section: a section; its gap is derived the same way
Page.rayl-stack: a group; its gap is what its largest text asks for
Page.rayl-grid: an even grid of cards or swatches
Page.rayl-head: a header or footer row: mark on the left, controls right
Page.rayl-card: a panel that lifts off the ground
Page.rayl-row: a named control on one line
Page.rayl-row-name: the name in that row — 12, Medium, full ink, sentence case
Page.rayl-label: the 8 uppercase section label, and nothing else
Page.rayl-hint: a quiet line of explanation under a block
Page.rayl-gap-6: set a group's gap when it has no heading to derive one

Wide layout.rayl-hero: the opening statement of a page
Wide layout.rayl-band: a full-width band; is-ink for one in ink
Wide layout.rayl-media: a picture that follows the column beside it

Document.rayl-doc: on the body: the document ground rather than the app one
Document.rayl-chapter: an 8 label on the ground, over the blocks under it
Document.rayl-rail-foot: pinned to the floor of a rail
Document.rayl-field: the things of a block, stacked 12 apart
Document.rayl-field-row: frames side by side inside a field
Document.rayl-frame: one white box holding one thing; is-tall, is-wide
Document.rayl-container: a plain white box for a header or footer

Controls.rayl-btn: the button; aria-pressed for on, data-icon for an icon
Controls.rayl-ibtn: the reveal button: the label contracts, a circle irises open
Controls.rayl-seg: the option group — exactly one on; is-joined, is-tight
Controls.rayl-seg-opt: one cell of it; is-on, is-third
Controls.rayl-seg-name: the name that opens a joined bar — never a disabled cell
Controls.rayl-slider: the track: data-min, data-max, data-val, data-step
Controls.rayl-line: a value on a line that rolls; data-label, data-swap
Controls.rayl-icon: an icon on its own; data-icon
Controls.rayl-solve: the loading mark: data-size, data-play, data-ease and the timings
Controls.rayl-btn is-strong: the one high-emphasis button — a dialog's confirm

Enterable surfaces.rayl-input: the field; is-multi for a textarea
Enterable surfaces.rayl-select: the select — author the options, it builds the rest
Enterable surfaces.rayl-menu: a list of items on its own ground
Enterable surfaces.rayl-menu-opt: one item of it; is-on for the chosen one
Enterable surfaces.rayl-check: the checkbox, carrying its own label; is-small for 12
Enterable surfaces.rayl-toggle: the switch; data-on and data-off name its two states

Surfaces and panels.rayl-modal: a dialog; data-opens and data-closes name it by id
Surfaces and panels.rayl-tip: a tooltip — put data-tip on the thing it labels
Surfaces and panels.rayl-popover: a card that arrives: 264 across, padding 12
Surfaces and panels.rayl-tabs: a rayl-seg bar over rayl-panel panels
Surfaces and panels.rayl-panel: the panel under a bar, or under anything
Surfaces and panels.rayl-fold: a collapsible section: a details, and a body
Surfaces and panels.rayl-table: a list of records; every other row is banded
Surfaces and panels.rayl-empty: a panel with nothing in it — and the error panel too
Surfaces and panels.rayl-skeleton: blocks where type will land; data-lines

Type.rayl-serif: Concrette, on a size class from 24 up

missing.a brief will ask for: a settings panel that comes in from an edge — the dialog ships, these do not
anything reporting that a background job finished
an export, an upload, a render — determinate, where the mark says nothing about how far
a right-click or an overflow: rayl-menu is the list, nothing opens one at a pointer
a count, a status, a filter
every panel taller than its frame
a control panel beside a canvas — the only layout the system cannot express
